operation.body:
## Goal
Implement the approved R-001 per-source session failure policy as a deterministic DiscoveryCore state machine, tested with synthetic outcomes before live collectors or scheduling are added.

## Acceptance criteria
- Model typed success, timeout, permission-denied, malformed-response and generic-error outcomes; no raw payload parsing or source calls.
- Timeout and denial disable the source immediately for the remainder of that policy instance/session. The first generic error or malformed response allows at most one retry at the next scheduled sample; a further failure without an intervening success disables it. Success clears the consecutive-failure budget while active; a disabled policy never reactivates on later outcomes.
- Expose the disposition and bounded typed cause for later collector integration; policy decisions cannot execute or schedule retries. Clearly document that the caller must wait for its next scheduled sample, that no deadline/worker cancellation guarantee exists and that a fresh policy instance is required per new source/session.
- Verify the outcome transition matrix, success reset, absorbing disabled state and independent source/session instances with fixture-only tests. Retain existing CLI refusal and all existing product/adapter checks.
- Update development and discovery specification status without claiming integration, live collection, full discovery or hardware safety. Run integrated review, signed PR handoff and CI; assess actual risk and auto-merge eligibility independently under existing policy.

## Constraints
Parent Project #1; owner's current local self-correcting-review auto-merge request authorizes exactly this one goal. Only Low-risk, otherwise eligible changes may agent-squash; all mandatory human-review and safety gates remain. Implements already accepted R-001 bounded failure handling (decision 6879220276), within the existing pure core. No new security/privacy boundary or externally visible CLI behavior. Preserve private workflow, historical reference and unrelated .gitlab/. Risks: retry logic accidentally used for immediate retries, reactivating disabled sources, confusing pure policy with implemented collector deadlines/cancellation. Decision queue: no blocking material choices; actual collector outcome mapping, sampling scheduler, deadlines/worker lifecycle and report integration stay separate.

## Out of scope
Hardware commands/tests, privilege, workloads, SMC, source/native calls, live sampling, timers, worker/IPC/cancellation, report/CLI integration, file/network access, persistence, full payload decoding, dependencies/toolchain changes, controller/GUI/recovery, background automation and a second Agent Goal.

## Relevant context
docs/discovery-specification.md collection bounds/failure rules; docs/development.md; .ai/docs/project-requirements.md; .ai/project/. All delegated goals 2,7,9,11,13 have merged PRs; no outstanding deferred-owner-validation marker. PR #14 was human-ready/merged by szymoniwacz as 923a2a8a5bff8bbf30d483b3f3ea02ac62a147c2; current main CI 43618402921 passed. Interrupted Goal #13 retained this same local session's exact owner token; check verified it and normal finish/drain returned RELEASED (generation 1, processed=requested=1). Completed read-only review worker was verified ended; no executor was bypassed or recovery/takeover performed. Project lock was acquired only after that release. Prior PR metadata update was interrupted by automatic approval-review usage limits, not a correctness failure; terminal Goal #13/PR #14 are not reopened or rewritten.

Rollback: reviewed forward revert PR; this state machine stores no data outside its instance and starts no service.
